# [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters


::: {.callout-warning}
THIS BOOK IS A WORK IN PROGRESS. IT IS INCOMPLETE AND MAY HAVE TYPOGRAPHICAL AND OTHER ERRORS.
IT IS NOT YET READY TO BE STUDIED FROM.
:::


## Introduction

There are some verbs that,
in addition to a doer,
also
generally require two direct doees.
[ظَنَّ]{.ar} is one of these verbs.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [Peled, _Sentence types_ 188]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be your brother.]{.trans}  

There are other verbs similar to [ظَنَّ]{.ar}.
We will study them collectively as "[ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters."

## The lean of the [ظَنَّ]{.ar} sentence

The basic nounal sentence consists of a subject and a info.
For example:

(@) [زَيْدٌ أَخُوكَ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd is your brother.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
is the subject
and
[أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
is its info.
Both are in the u-case because it is a basic nounal sentence.
In terms of its lean,
[زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
is the leaned-against element
and
[أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
is the leaning element.
(Technically, the leaning element is [أَخ]{.ar}. And it in turn is a annexed noun to the annexed-to noun [كَ]{.ar}.
But loosely speaking, we can say that the leaning element is the bundled [أَخُوكَ]{.ar}.)
With the leaned-against element and the leaning element in place, the sentence is leaned.

Now consider the following sentence:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [Peled, _Sentence types_ 188]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be your brother.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
the verb [ظَنَّ]{.ar}
takes the subject and info of example (),
and makes them into direct doees.
The verb [ظَنَّ]{.ar}
requires a doer (as usual),
which is the pronoun [تُ]{.ar} [I]{.trans}.
And it also requires two direct doees:
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
is the first direct doee
and
[أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
is the second direct doee.

This sentence is peculiar in its lean.
This is because the indispensable elements are the two direct doees.
[زَيْدًا]{.ar}
is the leaned-against element
and
[أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
is the leaning element.^[[البسيط لابن أبي الربيع]{.ar} 433]
The sentence is only leaned when both direct doees are in place.
Unlike normal verbal sentences,
the verb [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its doer are not the indispensable elements of the sentence.
Rather [ظَنَّ]{.ar} is the foundational government.
Figure () depicts the government of example ().

Parallels of the lean of the [ظَنَّ]{.ar} sentence
may be found in the [كَانَ]{.ar} and [إِنَّ]{.ar} sentences:

(@) [كَانَ زَيْدٌ أَخَاكَ]{.ar}
    [Peled, _Sentence types_ 188]{.citex}  
    [Zayd was your brother.]{.trans}  
    ([زَيْدٌ]{.ar}, the doer/subject, is the leaned-against element.
    [أَخَاكَ]{.ar}, the direct doee/info, is the leaning element.
    [كَانَ]{.ar} is the foundational government.)


(@) [إِنَّ زَيْدًا أَخُوكَ]{.ar}
    [Peled, _Sentence types_ 188]{.citex}  
    [Indeed Zayd is your brother.]{.trans}  
    ([زَيْدًا]{.ar}, the subject, is the leaned-against element.
    [أَخُوكَ]{.ar}, the info, is the leaning element.
    [إِنَّ]{.ar} is the foundational government.)

Similar to (deficient) [كَانَ]{.ar} sentences,
the [ظَنَّ]{.ar} sentence may be categorized as a verbal sentence.
And, like in the case of deficient [كَانَ]{.ar},
the verb and its doer don't make the sentence leaned.

## [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters in passive voice

When [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters are used in the passive voice,
the first direct doee
(the one which is the subject in the basic nounal sentence)
is made the deputy doer in the u-case.
And the second direct doee
(the one which is the info in the basic nounal sentence)
remains a direct doee in the a-case.
So, example () above, becomes in the passive voice:

(@) [ظُنَّ زَيْدٌ أَخَاكَ]{.ar}  
    [Zayd was thought to be your brother.]{.trans}

Similarly,

(@) [زَيْدٌ مَظْنُونٌ شُجَاعًا]{.ar}
    [Wright 2/52D]{.citex}  
    [Zayd is thought to be brave.]{.trans}  

##  The sisters of [ظَنَّ]{.ar}

There are many verbs that behave similar to [ظَنَّ]{.ar},
in that they require two direct doees.

In this chapter, we will refer to the first direct doee,
(the one which is the subject in the basic nounal sentence)
as _x_.
And we will refer to the second direct doee,
(the one which is the info in the basic nounal sentence)
as _y_.

These verbs constituting [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters may be sub-categorized into:

1. *Verbs of perception*. These verbs indicate that the doer believes the first direct doee to be something that is indicated by the second direct doee.
   For example:
   [ظَنَّ]{.ar} [to think, conjecture _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
   [عَلِمَ]{.ar} [to know _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
   [حَسِبَ]{.ar} [to deem, reckon _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
   [خَالَ]{.ar} [to imagine _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
   [زَعَمَ]{.ar} [to claim _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
   [رَأَىٰ]{.ar} [to opine _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
   and more.

2. *Verbs of rendering*. These verbs indicate that the doer changes or leaves the direct doee in a state that is indicated by the second direct doee.
   For example:
   [صَيَّرَ]{.ar} [to make _x_ become _y_]{.trans},
   [اتَّخَذَ]{.ar} [to take _x_ for oneself as _y_]{.trans},
   [تَرَكَ]{.ar} [to leave _x_ as _y_]{.trans},
   [جَعَلَ]{.ar} [to make _x_ into _y_]{.trans},
   and more.

Some verbs, like [جَعَلَ]{.ar} can fall into both categories, where [جَعَلَ]{.ar} can also mean [to believe _x_ to be _y_]{.trans}, in addition to [to make _x_ into _y_]{.trans}.

We will give examples of these verbs below:

### [ظَنَّ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

The basic meaning of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} is to believe,
with a variable range of conviction,
_x_ to be _y_.
Due to the conjectural nature of this meaning,
it can be used in a range of circumstances from
where its doer believes something to be certain,
to cases where he is doubtful.

Here are some examples:

(@) [وَإِنِّی لَأَظُنُّكَ یَـٰفِرۡعَوۡنُ مَثۡبُورࣰا]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الإسراء]{.ar} 17:102](https://quran.com/17/102) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/331]{.citex}  
    [and indeed I think, O Pharaoh, that you are destroyed.]{.trans}  

(@) [قُلۡتُم مَّا نَدۡرِی مَا ٱلسَّاعَةُ إِن نَّظُنُّ إِلَّا ظَنࣰّا وَمَا نَحۡنُ بِمُسۡتَیۡقِنِینَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الجاثية]{.ar} 45:32](https://quran.com/45/32) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/331]{.citex}  
    [you said, 'We know not what is the Hour. We assume only assumption, and we are not convinced.']{.trans}  

(@) [ظَنَنْتُكَ إِنْ شَبَّتْ لَظَى الْحَرْبِ صَالِيًا]{.ar}
    [cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/331]{.citex}  
    [I thought you, if the blaze of war is kindled, to be entering (therein)]{.trans}  

[ظَنَّ]{.ar} following examples is interpreted to have certainty in its meaning:

(@) [قَالَ ٱلَّذِینَ یَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَـٰقُوا۟ ٱللَّهِ كَم مِّن فِئَةࣲ قَلِیلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةࣰ كَثِیرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّـٰبِرِینَ]{.quran}^[See [[تفسير ابن عثيمين]{.ar} for [سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:249](https://tafsir.app/ibn-uthaymeen/2/249)]
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:249](https://quran.com/2/249) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/332]{.citex}  
    [But those who were certain that they would meet Allāh said, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allāh. And Allāh is with the patient."]{.trans}

(@) [إِنِّی ظَنَنتُ أَنِّی مُلَـٰقٍ حِسَابِیَهۡ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الحاقة]{.ar} 69:20](https://quran.com/69/20) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/332]{.citex}  
    [Indeed, I was certain that I would be meeting my account."]{.trans}  

(@) [وَرَءَا ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ ٱلنَّارَ فَظَنُّوۤا۟ أَنَّهُم مُّوَاقِعُوهَا وَلَمۡ یَجِدُوا۟ عَنۡهَا مَصۡرِفࣰا]{.quran}^[See [[تفسير ابن عثيمين]{.ar} for [سورة الكهف]{.ar} 18:53](https://tafsir.app/ibn-uthaymeen/18/53)]
    [[[سورة الكهف]{.ar} 18:53](https://quran.com/18/53) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/332]{.citex}  
    [And the criminals will see the Fire and will be certain that they are to fall therein. And they will not find from it a way elsewhere.]{.trans}  

As to the usage of [أَنَّ]{.ar} in the examples above, see @sec:ta3leeq below.

[ظَنَّ]{.ar} can also have the meaning of [to suspect (someone)]{.trans}.
With this meaning, it is no longer a verb of perception,
and will only need one direct doee.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَّ القَاضِي فُلَانًا]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/331]{.citex}  
    [The judge suspected so-and-so.]{.trans}  

### [عَلِمَ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

[عَلِمَ]{.ar} means [to know]{.trans}.
Examples:

(@) [عَلِمْتُكَ الْبَاذِلَ الْمَعْرُوفَ]{.ar}
    [Wright 2/49B]{.citex}  
    [I have known you to be liberal in the exercise of bounty.]{.trans}  

(@) [فَإِنۡ **عَلِمۡتُمُوهُنَّ مُؤۡمِنَـٰتࣲ** فَلَا تَرۡجِعُوهُنَّ إِلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِۖ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الممتحنة]{.ar} 60:10](https://quran.com/60/10) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/325]{.citex}  
    [And if **you know them to be believers**, then do not return them to the disbelievers;]{.trans}  

When [عَلِمَ]{.ar} has only the meaning
[to know (something)]{.trans}
and not
[to know (something) to be (something)]{.trans}
then it may take only one direct doee.
For example:

(@) [وَٱللَّهُ أَخۡرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمۡ **لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ شَیۡـࣰٔا**]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النحل]{.ar} 16:78](https://quran.com/16/78) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/236]{.citex}  
    [And Allāh has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers **not knowing a thing**]{.trans}  

(@) [لَقَدْ **عَلِمْتُ النَّظَائِرَ** الَّتِي كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهِنَّ سُورَتَيْنِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :822e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:822e)]{.citex}  
    [**I know the manners** in which the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} recited two [sUrah]{.trn2}s in one [rakeah]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  

### [رَأَىٰ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

### [حَسِبَ]{.ar} {.unnumbered}

(@) [صَنَعْنَا لِرَسُولِ اللهِ ﷺ فَخَّارَةً ، فَأَتَيْتُهُ بِهَا ، فَوَضَعْتُهَا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ، فَاطَّلَعَ فِيهَا ، فَقَالَ : **حَسِبْتُهُ لَحْمًا**]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :14581](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:14581)]{.citex}  
    [We made a (clay) pot (of food) for the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} and I brought it to him. He peered into it and said, "**I thought it was meat.**"]{.trans}  

## The second direct doee can be a sentence or phrase

Because [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters govern
what was originally a subject-info sentence,
the first direct doee may be anything which is allowed to be a subject,
and
the second direct doee may be anything which is allowed to be a info.
Thus, the second direct doee
may be a complete sentence in the positional a-case,
or an adverbial or prepositional phrase.^[[@baseet_ibn_abi_rabee3 443](https://archive.org/details/0969pdf_201912/page/n441/mode/2up)]

Here are some examples
where the second direct doee is a complete sentence:

(@) [**مَا عَلِمْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم نَكَحَ** شَيْئًا مِنْ نِسَائِهِ وَلاَ أَنْكَحَ شَيْئًا مِنْ بَنَاتِهِ عَلَى أَكْثَرَ مِنْ ثِنْتَىْ عَشْرَةَ أُوقِيَّةً]{.ar}
    [[[جامع الترمذي]{.ar} :1114b](https://sunnah.com/tirmidhi:1114b)]{.citex}  
    [**I did not know the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} to marry** any of his women, nor to give any of his daughters in marriage, for more than twelve [#Uqiyah]{.trn2}s.]{.trans}  
    (First direct doee is [رَسُول الله]{.ar} [the Messenger of Allāh]{.trans}, second direct doee is [نَكَحَ]{.ar} [he married]{.trans}.)

(@) [**مَا عَلِمْتُهُ صَامَ** شَهْرًا كُلَّهُ إِلاَّ رَمَضَانَ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :1156b](https://sunnah.com/muslim:1156b)]{.citex}  
    [**I did not know him to fast** any complete month except [#ramaDAn]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  
    (First direct doee is [هُ]{.ar} [him]{.trans}, second direct doee is [صَامَ]{.ar} [he fasted]{.trans}.)

(@) [**ظَنَنْتُهُ يَدْعُو** فِي الِاسْتِسْقَاءِ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح ابن خزيمة]{.ar} :1595](https://hadithunlocked.com/ibnkhuzaymah:1595)]{.citex}
    [**I thought him to be supplicating** in the rain prayer.]{.trans}  
    (First direct doee is [هُ]{.ar} [him]{.trans}, second direct doee is [يَدْعُو]{.ar} [supplicating]{.trans}.)

Here is an example
where the second direct doee is a prepositional phrase:

(@) [قَالَ أَمَا وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لِتَغَيُّرِ ثَائِرَةٍ كَانَتْ مِنِّي إِلَيْهِمْ وَلَكِنِّي **أَرَاهُمْ عَلَى ضَلَالَةٍ**]{.ar}
    [[[مستدرك الحاكم]{.ar} :4956](https://hadithunlocked.com/hakim:4956)]{.citex}  
    [He said, "By Allāh, indeed that is because of a change in a matter between me and them, but **I think them to be on misguidance**."]{.trans}  
    (First direct doee is [هُمْ]{.ar} [them]{.trans}, second direct doee is [عَلَى ضَلَالٍ]{.ar} [on misguidance]{.trans}.)

## When two direct doees are not required

Many of the verbs in [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters
may be used with meanings
such that they don't govern
what was originally a subject-info sentence.
In such cases, the two indispensable elements are
the verb and its doer,
and the verb does not require two direct doees to be the indispensable elements.

For example,
[ظَنَّ]{.ar} can have the meaning
[to suspect (someone)]{.trans}.
With this meaning,
can take one direct doee.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَّ القَاضِي فُلَانًا]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/331]{.citex}  
    [The judge suspected so-and-so.]{.trans}  

(@) [عُدِمَ لِي مَالٌ فَظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [[Howell §442 2/150](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=211)]{.citex}  
    [Some property of mine was missing so I suspected Zayd.]{.trans}  

Similarly
[عَلِمَ]{.ar}
can be used with the meaning
[to know _x_]{.trans}
and not necessarily
[to know _x_ to be _y_]{.trans}.
For example:

(@) [وَٱللَّهُ أَخۡرَجَكُم مِّنۢ بُطُونِ أُمَّهَـٰتِكُمۡ **لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ شَیۡـࣰٔا**]{.quran}
    [[[سورة النحل]{.ar} 16:78](https://quran.com/16/78) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/236]{.citex}  
    [And Allāh has extracted you from the wombs of your mothers **not knowing a thing**]{.trans}  

(@) [لَقَدْ **عَلِمْتُ النَّظَائِرَ** الَّتِي كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ بِهِنَّ سُورَتَيْنِ فِي رَكْعَةٍ]{.ar}
    [[[صحيح مسلم]{.ar} :822e](https://sunnah.com/muslim:822e)]{.citex}  
    [**I know the manners** in which the Messenger of Allāh [ﷺ]{.areng} recited two [sUrah]{.trn2}s in one [rakeah]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  

[رَأَىٰ]{.ar}
can mean
[to opine _x_]{.trans}
and not necessarily
[to opine _x_ to be _y_]{.trans}.
For example:

(@) [رَأَىٰ أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ حِلَّ كَذَا]{.ar}
    [[Howell §442 2/150](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=211)]{.citex}  
    [[#abU #HanIfah]{.trn2} held (the opinion of) the lawfulness of such a thing.]{.trans}

[رَأَىٰ]{.ar}
can also simply mean [to see _x_]{.trans}.
For example:

(@) [رَأَيْتُهُ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §442 2/150](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=211)]{.citex}  
    [I saw him]{.trans}  

When [رَأَىٰ]{.ar} has the meaning [to see]{.trans},
then there may be a second a-case (indefinite) governee as a [HAl]{.trn2}.^[[البسيط لابن أبي الربيع]{.ar} 445]
For example:

(@) [رَأَيْتُ زَيْدًا ضَاحِكًا]{.ar}
    [[البسيط لابن أبي الربيع]{.ar} 445]{.citex}  
    [I saw Zayd laughing.]{.trans}  

<!--
If,
[رَأَىٰ]{.ar} has the meaning [to see]{.trans},
but it also includes the meaning [to know]{.trans}
then [رَأَى]{.ar} can take two direct doees.^[[البسيط لابن أبي الربيع]{.ar} 447; [[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/327](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/723); [[الدر المصون للسمين الحلبي]{.ar} for [سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:4](https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/12/4)]
-->
If, however,
[رَأَىٰ]{.ar} has the meaning [to see _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
then it will take two direct doees.^[See also [البسيط لابن أبي الربيع]{.ar} 447; [[شرح التسهيل لابن مالك]{.ar} 2/327](https://shamela.ws/book/13257/723); [[الدر المصون للسمين الحلبي]{.ar} for [سورة يوسف]{.ar} 12:4](https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/12/4)]
For example:

(@) [يَا مَعْشَرَ النِّسَاءِ تَصَدَّقْنَ وَأَكْثِرْنَ فَإِنِّي **رَأَيْتُكُنَّ أَكْثَرَ أَهْلِ النَّارِ** لِكَثْرَةِ اللَّعْنِ وَكُفْرِ الْعَشِيرِ]{.ar}
    [[[مسند أحمد]{.ar} :5343](https://hadithunlocked.com/ahmad:5343) cited by [البسيط لابن أبي الربيع]{.ar} 447 footnote 1]{.citex}  
    [O women, give charity and do a lot of it, for indeed **I saw you to be the majority of the people of the Fire**, because of much cursing [on your part] and being ungrateful to the husband.]{.trans}  

Besides the above,
other sisters of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} may have similar meanings as well.

## Suppressing one or both direct doees

Generally speaking,
for verbs
that take two direct doees,
but are
not in [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters,
we may restrict ourselves to only one direct doee.
So, for example, instead of saying:

(@) [أَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا دِرْهَمًا]{.ar}  
    [I gave Zayd a dirham.]{.trans}

we can say both:

(@) [أَعْطَيْتُ دِرْهَمًا]{.ar}  
    [[Howell §443 2/152](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=213)]{.citex}  
    [I gave a dirham.]{.trans}

(@) [أَعْطَيْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}  
    [[Howell §443 2/152](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=213)]{.citex}  
    [I gave Zayd.]{.trans}

But if the verb is one of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} or its sisters,
and they govern what was originally a subject-info sentence,
then both mafulbs are generally required.
So, for example, instead of saying:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}

we cannot say (generally):

(@) ✗ [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}

(@) ✗ [ظَنَنْتُ قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}

However, it is possible to omit one of the two direct doees
if its meaning is implied and is indicated by context.^[[Howell §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]
For example,

(@) [وَلَا **یَحۡسَبَنَّ** ٱلَّذِینَ یَبۡخَلُونَ بِمَاۤ ءَاتَىٰهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ **هُوَ خَیۡرࣰا لَّهُمۖ**]{.quran}
    [[[سورة آل عمران]{.ar} 3:180](https://quran.com/3/180) cited by [Howell §443 2/153--154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)^[cited as III. 175]]{.citex}  
    [And let not those who [greedily] withhold what Allāh has given them of His bounty **ever think that it is better for them**.]{.trans}

In the [Ayah]{.trn2} above,
the first direct doee of
[يَحْسَبَنَّ]{.ar}
is interpreted
(in one interpretation of this reading)
to be a suppressed [بُخْلَهُمْ]{.ar}
[their miserliness]{.trans},
and [هُوَ]{.ar} is a separating-pronoun.
Such that the meaning is:

(@) [ولا يَحْسَبَنَّ الباخِلون **بُخْلَهم** هو خيرًا لهم]{.ar}
    [[[الدر المصون للسمين الحلبي]{.ar} for [سورة آل عمران]{.ar} 3:180](https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/3/180)]{.citex}  
    [And let not the misers think **their miserliness** to be good for them.]{.trans}

Both direct doees can also be omitted together.
For example:

(@) [وَظَنَنتُمۡ ظَنَّ ٱلسَّوۡءِ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الفتح]{.ar} 48:12](https://quran.com/48/12) cited by [Howell §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [And you assumed an assumption of evil]{.trans}  
    ([ظَنَّ]{.ar} is analyzed to be a absolute doee.^[[[إعراب القرآن للدرويش]{.ar} for [سورة الفتح]{.ar} 48:12](https://tafsir.app/iraab-aldarweesh/48/12)])  

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ ذَاكَ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}  
    [I thought that.]{.trans}  
    ([ذَاكَ]{.ar} is a deputy to the [maSdar]{.trn2} as the absolute doee.)

(@) [مَنْ يَسْمَعْ يَخَلْ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [Whoso hears, will think.]{.trans}  

The preposition [بِ]{.ar} may be used with [ظَنَّ]{.ar} to mean [about]{.trans}.
In this case as well, no direct doee is needed.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ بِهِ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/154](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=215)]{.citex}  
    [I thought about him.]{.trans}

Even in such cases where both direct doees are omitted,
their meaning may be implied.
For example:

(@) [وَیَوۡمَ یُنَادِیهِمۡ فَیَقُولُ أَیۡنَ شُرَكَاۤءِیَ ٱلَّذِینَ **كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ**]{.quran}
    [[[سورة القصص]{.ar} 28:62](https://quran.com/28/62) cited by [Howell §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [And [warn of] the Day He will call them and say, "Where are My 'partners' which **you used to claim**?"]{.trans}  

In the [Ayah]{.trn2} above, the two suppressed direct doees of [تَزْعُمُونَ]{.ar}
are interpreted to be thus:

(@) [تَزْعُمُونَهُمْ شُرَكَاءَ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §443 2/153](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=214)]{.citex}  
    [...\ you claim them to be partners]{.trans}


## Suspension of government

There are sentences in which
the verbs of perception were to exercise their
governing effect
on a subject and info.
But their direct government
is _suspended_ due to the presence of a _preventer_
which exercises its own effect
on the subject and info.
This phenomenon is called
_suspension_ of government.
Let's take a look at an example.
Consider a sentence where [ظَنَّ]{.ar} exercises it governing effect.

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا قَائِمًا]{.ar}
    [I thought Zayd to be standing.]{.trans}  

Now let's see what happens when the
original
subject
([زَيْد]{.ar})
and info
([قَائِم]{.ar})
are preceded by a [لَ]{.ar} of beginning.
The sentence becomes:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/158](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=219)]{.citex}  
    [I thought, assuredly Zayd is standing.]{.trans}  

As you can see,
the
original
subject
([زَيْد]{.ar})
and info
([قَائِم]{.ar})
are now both in the u-case.
This is because the effect of the [لَ]{.ar} of beginning
is to cause a
subject
and info
to be in the u-case.
The government of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} is thus suspended.
The inner sentence
[لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
is said to be in the positional a-case
as a direct doee of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} that fulfils the role of two direct doees.

The proof that the inner sentence
[لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
is in the positional a-case
and that the government of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} is suspended,
is that if we were to put a conjunction after this sentence,
then the governing effect of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} would resume.
For example:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ لَزَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ **وَعَمْرًا مُنْطَلِقًا**]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/158](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=219)]{.citex}  
    [I thought, assuredly Zayd is standing **and [#eamr]{.trn2} is setting out**.]{.trans}  

The preventers that suspend the government of
the verbs of perception are discussed in the subsections below:

### The negaters [مَا]{.ar}, [إِنْ]{.ar}, and [لَا]{.ar}

Examples:

(@) [لَقَدۡ عَلِمۡتَ مَا هَـٰۤؤُلَاۤءِ یَنطِقُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الأنبياء]{.ar} 21:65](https://quran.com/21/65) cited by [النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/346; [Howell §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    ["You have already known that these do not speak!"]{.trans}  

In example () above, the negater [مَا]{.ar} prevents [عَلِمْتَ]{.ar} from
directly governing two direct doees. Instead,
the sentence
[مَا هَؤُلَاءِ يَنْطِقُونَ]{.ar}
is in the positional a-case as a direct doee
that fulfils the role two direct doees.

(@) [عَلِمْتُ وَاللهِ إِنْ زَيْدٌ قَائِمٌ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [I knew, by Allāh, Zayd is not standing.]{.trans}  

(@) [عَلِمْتُ وَاللهِ لَا زَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ ولَا عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [I knew, by Allāh, Zayd is not in the house, nor [#eamr]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  


### [لَ]{.ar} of beginning

We have already seen in example () above, how [لَ]{.ar} of beginning suspends
the direct government of a verb of perception.
Here is another example:

(@) [وَلَقَدۡ **عَلِمُوا۟ لَمَنِ** ٱشۡتَرَىٰهُ مَا لَهُۥ فِی ٱلۡـَٔاخِرَةِ مِنۡ خَلَـٰقࣲۚ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة البقرة]{.ar} 2:102](https://quran.com/2/102) cited by [Howell §445 2/160](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=221)]{.citex}  
    [But **they [i.e., the Children of Israel] certainly knew that whoever** purchased it [i.e., magic] would not have in the Hereafter any share.]{.trans}  


### [لَ]{.ar} of oath

(@) [لَقدْ عَلِمْتُ لَتَأْتِيَنَّ مَنِيَّتِي ~ إِنَّ الْمَنَايًا لَا تَطِيشُ سِهَامُهَا]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/346; [Howell §445 2/158](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=219)]{.citex}  
    [And assuredly, I have known (by God) verily my fate will come. Verily the fates---their arrows do not miss.]{.trans}  

The presence of the [لَ]{.ar} of oath in 
[لَتَأْتِيَنَّ]{.ar}
suspends the direct government of [عَلِمْتُ]{.ar}.
Otherwise the sentence would have been:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ مَنِيَّتِي آتِيَةً]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/436]{.citex}  
    [I have known my fate to be coming.]{.trans}  

### A question sentence

A question sentence can follow
a verb of perception
and in such a case
the government of the verb of perception
is suspended
if the entire question sentence
is its direct doee.

Here is an example:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ أَزَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ أَمْ عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew whether Zayd was in the house or [#eamr]{.trn2}.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
the entire question sentence
[أَزَيْدٌ فِي الدَّارِ أَمْ عَمْرٌو]{.ar}
is in the a-case
and it fulfils the role the two direct doees of [عَلِمْتُ]{.ar}.
That is the traditional explanation.
However, it is also possible that
[عَلِمَ]{.ar} here is with the meaning [to know _x_]{.trans}
in which case the question sentence
fulfils the role the one required direct doee.

Another point to note is that the question sentence
is now no longer a question to the listener.
That is why we have not puntuated the translation with a question mark (?).
Rather, the entire example sentence
is signifying that the speaker knows the answer to the question.

Here is another example:

(@) [وَلَتَعۡلَمُنَّ أَیُّنَاۤ أَشَدُّ عَذَابࣰا وَأَبۡقَىٰ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة طه]{.ar} 20:71](https://quran.com/20/71) cited by [Howell §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [and you will surely know which of us is more severe in [giving] punishment and more enduring]{.trans}

In example () above,
there are three possible interpretations^[[[الدر المصون للسمين الحلبي]{.ar} for [سورة طه]{.ar} 20:71](https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/20/71)]:

a. The first interpretation, and the one relevant to our discussion here,
   is that [أَيّ]{.ar} is a subject and [أَشَدّ]{.ar} is its info.
   The question sentence
   [أَیُّنَا أَشَدُّ عَذَابًا وَأَبْقَىٰ]{.ar}
   fulfils the role the two direct doees of [تَعْلَمُنَّ]{.ar}.
b. Another interpretation is [تَعْلَمُنَّ]{.ar} here only requires one direct doee
   and the question sentence is that (positional) direct doee.
c. A third interpretation is that [أَيّ]{.ar} is a connected noun.
   [أَيّ]{.ar} itself (not the entire question sentence) is the direct doee of
   [تَعْلَمُنَّ]{.ar}.
   And [أَيّ]{.ar} is inflexible ending with a [Dammah]{.trn2} because of a phenomenon described in @sec:mabny_ayy.

Here are some more examples:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ مَتَىٰ السَّفَرُ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew when the journey was (or would be).]{.trans}

(@) [عَلِمْتُ أَبُو مَنْ زَيْدٌ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew whose father was Zayd.]{.trans}

(@) [عَلِمْتُ صَبِيحَةَ أَيِّ يَوْمٍ سَفَرُكَ]{.ar}
    [[Howell §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [I knew the morning of which day your journey was (or will be).]{.trans}

(@) [وَسَیَعۡلَمُ ٱلَّذِینَ ظَلَمُوۤا۟ أَیَّ مُنقَلَبࣲ یَنقَلِبُونَ]{.quran}
    [[[سورة الشعراء]{.ar} 26:227](https://quran.com/26/227) cited by [Howell §445 2/159](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=220)]{.citex}  
    [And those who have wronged are going to know to what [kind of] return they will be returned.]{.trans}  

In example () above, [أَيّ]{.ar} is a question-device in the a-case as a absolute doee, governed by [يَنْقَلِبُونَ]{.ar}.^[[[الدر المصون للسمين الحلبي]{.ar} for [سورة الشعراء]{.ar} 26:227](https://tafsir.app/aldur-almasoon/26/227)]
The entire question sentence is in the a-case governed by [سَيَعْلَمُ]{.ar}.

#### Which verbs can precede question questions {.unnumbered}

verbs of knowledge: get examples from howell §445.

سأل and نظر etc. nahw_arabi 1/347

#### Interpretating a question-device vs a connected noun {.unnumbered}

We saw in example () above that
[أَيّ]{.ar} could be interpreted as a question-device
or as a connected noun.
This can be done with the other general connected nouns as well
like [مَنْ]{.ar} and [مَا]{.ar}.
But there can be a difference in meaning when one interpretation is chosen over the other.^[[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 2/37](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/420)]
Consider the following sentence:

(@) [عَلِمْتُ مَنْ قَامَ]{.ar}
    [[[معاني النحو]{.ar} 2/37](https://shamela.ws/book/17801/420) citing [شرح الرضي على الكافية]{.ar}]{.citex}  
    [I knew who stood.]{.trans}

If you choose to interpret [مَنْ]{.ar} as an connected noun,
then you are saying that the person who stood was known to you.
As if to say, "I am familiar with the person who stood."
[مَنْ]{.ar} in this case is (itself) the direct doee of [عَلِمْتُ]{.ar}.

And
if you choose to interpret [مَنْ]{.ar} as an question-device,
then you are saying that you knew the answer of the question, "Who stood?"
So you could pick him out of a line-up.
But you are not necessarily saying that you know, or are familiar with, that person.
The entire question sentence in this case is the direct doee of [عَلِمْتُ]{.ar}.

FIXME: move to istifham chapter:

Similarly, consider:

(@) [سَلْ أَيُّهُمْ قَامَ]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/347]{.citex}  
    [Ask: which of them stood?]{.trans}  

When [أَيّ]{.ar} is a question-device then
you are commanding someone to ask the question, "Which of them stood?"
But if you say, with [أَيّ]{.ar} in the a-case:

(@) [سَلْ أَيَّهُمْ قَامَ]{.ar}
    [[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/347]{.citex}  
    [Ask the one of them who stood.]{.trans}  

then you are commanding someone to interrogate the person (amongst a group of people) who stood.^[[النحو العربي: أحكام ومعان]{.ar} 1/347]

### Which verbs' government is subject to suspension?

From the verbs which comprise [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters,
suspension of government is limited to the flexible of the verbs of perception.
So the verbs of rendering like ... do not undergo suspension,
nor the rigid of the verbs of perception like ...

Additional verbs:
Howell §445 2/164

## Neutralization of government

Consider the following sentence:

(@) [ظَنَنْتُ زَيْدًا عَالِمًا]{.ar}
    [[Howell §444 2/155](https://adamiturabi.github.io/howell-navigator/content/2-07-0.html?page=216)]{.citex}  
    [I thought Zayd to be knowledgeable.]{.trans}  

In example () above,
[ظَنَّ]{.ar} is governing the subject ([زَيْد]{.ar})
and info ([عَالِم]{.ar})
as usual.

Now

Sometimes
[ظَنَّ]{.ar} (or its sisters)
occur in a sentence that has a subject and info,
and the meaning is of a verb of perception,
i.e. [to think _x_ to be _y_]{.trans},
but [ظَنَّ]{.ar}
(in such a sentence) does not directly govern the subject and info.

## [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters without two direct doees

[ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters
only require two direct doees
(as the two indispensable elements)
when [ظَنَّ]{.ar} (or its sisters)
operate on,
what was originally, a
subject-info sentence.

When such is not the case,
then [ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters do not require two direct doees.

[[تفسير ابن عاشور]{.ar} for [سورة الأحزاب]{.ar} 33:10](https://tafsir.app/ibn-aashoor/33/10)

##  suspension and neutralization

[ظَنَّ]{.ar} and its sisters are often found in sentences,
where there are two two nouns that have a subject-info relationship,
but they are not direct doees of [ظَنَّ]{.ar} (or its sisters).
